name: Trade war & tariffs
value: Trump threatens to double Mexico tariffs
summary: Trump threatened on 12 Nov to double tariffs on Mexican goods unless Mexico stops a migrant caravan
state: On 12 Nov President Trump threatened to immediately double tariffs on Mexican goods, including the Section 232 duties on steel, aluminium and vehicles that Mexico is negotiating to reduce, unless Mexico stops a caravan of about 1,500 migrants that left Tapachula on 10 Nov (Mexico News Daily). President Sheinbaum said Mexico would rely on persuasion, not force. The Yale Budget Lab updated its tracker of US tariffs on 9 Nov. Watch holds: a major tariff increase has been threatened but not yet imposed.
for_you: Importers and manufacturers with US–Mexico supply chains, especially in steel, aluminium and cars, are most exposed if the threat is carried out. Prices of affected goods tend to follow tariff changes with a lag.
rubric_hit: Watch: new major tariffs threatened between large economies (US threat on 12 Nov to double tariffs on Mexico)

sources.title: Mexico News Daily — Trump threatens to double tariffs on Mexico as a new migrant caravan heads north in Chiapas
Yale Budget Lab — The State of U.S. Tariffs

why: Tariffs raise prices, reroute supply chains and slow growth; escalation cycles hurt export-heavy economies like the UK's partners.
drivers: US tariff policy, retaliation, court rulings, trade deals, WTO disputes.

rubric.alert: Broad new tariffs in force with retaliation under way, or US average effective tariff rising sharply.
rubric.watch: New major tariffs announced or threatened between large economies.
rubric.normal: Tariff regime stable; no new major measures in the past two weeks.
